title: Heat Pump SHUT OFF Temp with AUX HEAT!
summary: An HVAC channel discusses whether to lock out a heat pump below a set outdoor temperature when electric auxiliary heat runs.

assertions.quote: the majority of those types of systems with electric backup do not shut off based on what the outdoor temperature is
there is no cookie cutter answer when we're talking about balance point

verdicts.note: The balance point depends on the home's heat loss and the unit's capacity curve, both of which vary by house.
The changeover temperature depends on house load and system size; the project chose 10F for warmer metro/southern homes and 5F for colder ones, targeting about 80% of load met.

assertions.quote: We're seeing markets and climates that these systems are being installed in and saving folks energy
you're going to see more and more systems on the market that don't have any backup heat at all

verdicts.note: Some cold-climate units are installed without strips in moderate climates, but most cold-region installs still include backup heat.

assertions.quote: if it gets so cold outside that the heat pump is basically rendered useless
